sentences.en: This is Hidden Brain.
sentences.zh: 这里是《隐藏的大脑》。

sentences.en: I'm Shankar Vedantam.
sentences.zh: 我是尚卡尔·维丹塔姆。

sentences.en: Today we have a story that will change the way you think about many things.
sentences.zh: 今天我们要讲一个故事，它将改变你对许多事物的看法。

sentences.en: Poverty, loneliness, time, even hunger.
sentences.zh: 贫困、孤独、时间，甚至是饥饿。

sentences.en: It's a tale about the psychological phenomenon of scarcity.
sentences.zh: 这是一个关于“稀缺”这一心理现象的故事。

sentences.en: It affects nearly everything in our lives and connects people who appear to have nothing in common.
sentences.zh: 它影响着我们生活中几乎方方面面，并将那些看似毫无共同点的人联系在一起。

sentences.en: The story of scarcity is a story of how not having enough of what you need can become the only thing that matters to you.
sentences.zh: 稀缺的故事，讲述的是当你急需的东西不足时，它如何成为你唯一在乎的事情。

sentences.en: My name is Brandi Drew.
sentences.zh: 我叫布兰迪·德鲁。

sentences.en: I'm from Detroit, Michigan.
sentences.zh: 我来自密歇根州底特律。

sentences.en: Brandi Drew has a story that may sound familiar to you.
sentences.zh: 布兰迪·德鲁的故事，或许听起来让你感到熟悉。

sentences.en: A story of poverty and debt.
sentences.zh: 一个关于贫困与债务的故事。

sentences.en: It's the kind of story that may lead people to quick conclusions.
sentences.zh: 这类故事往往容易让人草率下结论。

sentences.en: So pay attention to your own.
sentences.zh: 所以，请审视一下你自己的想法。

sentences.en: Brandi is now 37.
sentences.zh: 布兰迪今年37岁。

sentences.en: Six years ago, her life unraveled.
sentences.zh: 六年前，她的生活陷入了混乱。

sentences.en: At the time, she ran the dining services department at a senior living facility.
sentences.zh: 当时，她在一家养老院负责餐饮服务部门。

sentences.en: She'd been with a company that ran it for more than a decade.
sentences.zh: 她在那家承包餐饮的公司工作了十多年。

sentences.en: One day, she made a mistake.
sentences.zh: 有一天，她犯了一个错误。

sentences.en: I was just in a rush to get home, that was all.
sentences.zh: 我当时只是急着回家，仅此而已。

sentences.en: Because daycare closes at 6, I get off at 5.
sentences.zh: 因为托儿所6点关门，我5点下班。

sentences.en: It was like maybe a 10-mile drive, busy traffic area.
sentences.zh: 开车大概要10英里，路况很拥堵。

sentences.en: And I knew I had to pick up diapers.
sentences.zh: 我知道我得去买尿布。

sentences.en: And the easiest thing for me, I thought, would be to pick them up before I picked the baby up.
sentences.zh: 我想最省事的方法就是在接孩子之前先把尿布买好。

sentences.en: So Brandi stopped at a store, ran in, and grabbed the diapers.
sentences.zh: 于是布兰迪在一家商店停下，跑进去拿了尿布。

sentences.en: She swiped her credit card at the self-checkout station and raced out.
sentences.zh: 她在自助结账台刷了信用卡，然后匆匆离开。

sentences.en: It turns out, she used the wrong card.
sentences.zh: 结果发现，她用错了卡。

sentences.en: Not her own, but the company credit card.
sentences.zh: 不是她自己的卡，而是公司的信用卡。

sentences.en: But what's crazy is I didn't realize at that moment, I didn't realize until my supervisor called me in and said,
sentences.zh: 最疯狂的是，我当时根本没意识到，直到主管把我叫去说：

sentences.en: Hey, what's this purchase?
sentences.zh: “嘿，这笔消费是怎么回事？”

sentences.en: So had she not said anything, I don't think I would have realized that.
sentences.zh: 如果她没提，我想我根本不会发现。

sentences.en: Brandi carried the card in case she needed to buy dining supplies for work.
sentences.zh: 布兰迪随身带着这张卡，以备工作需要购买餐饮用品时使用。

sentences.en: She'd never had a problem before, never been reprimanded.
sentences.zh: 她以前从未出过问题，也从未受过训斥。

sentences.en: She thought an apology and an explanation would do.
sentences.zh: 她以为道个歉、解释一下就行了。

sentences.en: And her response was, well, you know, we have to terminate you.
sentences.zh: 但对方的回答是：“嗯，你知道的，我们必须解雇你。”

sentences.en: And I'm like, no, I didn't know that.
sentences.zh: 我说：“不，我不知道。”

sentences.en: Like, can I just pay you back?
sentences.zh: 我说：“我能把钱还给你吗？”

sentences.en: It was only, what, 12 bucks?
sentences.zh: 那才多少钱，12美元？

sentences.en: And she said, no, in cases like that, you automatically have to terminate the employee.
sentences.zh: 她说：“不行，在这种情况下，我们必须自动解雇员工。”

sentences.en: I just cried.
sentences.zh: 我当时就哭了。

sentences.en: I cried for like a whole day because I couldn't believe it.
sentences.zh: 我哭了一整天，因为我简直不敢相信。

sentences.en: I didn't want to go home and tell my kids what had happened.
sentences.zh: 我不想回家告诉孩子们发生了什么。

sentences.en: I didn't want to tell my husband what had happened.
sentences.zh: 我不想告诉丈夫发生了什么。

sentences.en: I just didn't know what to do at that point.
sentences.zh: 那一刻，我真的不知道该怎么办。

sentences.en: I felt like a failure as a parent because I didn't provide a good example, even though it was a mistake.
sentences.zh: 我觉得自己是个失败的母亲，因为我没能树立好榜样，尽管那只是个失误。

sentences.en: Brandi earned more than her husband, so the loss of the job hit hard.
sentences.zh: 布兰迪的收入比丈夫高，所以失业对她打击很大。

sentences.en: She felt like a loser.
sentences.zh: 她觉得自己是个失败者。

sentences.en: She tried to bring in money doing odd jobs like cooking takeaway meals, but the stress grew.
sentences.zh: 她试图通过做些零工，比如做外卖餐来赚钱，但压力越来越大。

sentences.en: Brandi and her husband began fighting.
sentences.zh: 布兰迪和丈夫开始争吵。

sentences.en: She had supported him when he'd been laid off a few years earlier, and she'd expected he'd do the same for her.
sentences.zh: 几年前他被裁员时，她曾支持过他，她本以为他也会这样对待她。

sentences.en: But he felt a layoff was different.
sentences.zh: 但他觉得裁员的情况不一样。

sentences.en: He was mad that she'd made a stupid mistake.
sentences.zh: 他很生气，因为她犯了那种愚蠢的错误。

sentences.en: The final argument was that I left off the house that morning.
sentences.zh: 最后一次争吵是因为那天早上我出门了。

sentences.en: I was going to job interviews.
sentences.zh: 我去参加面试。

sentences.en: I had two interviews that day, and I didn't purchase toilet paper.
sentences.zh: 那天我有两场面试，结果没买卫生纸。

sentences.en: So when he got home from work that day, there was no toilet paper.
sentences.zh: 所以他下班回家时，家里没有卫生纸了。

sentences.en: When I came in with the kids, he just immediately started yelling,
sentences.zh: 当我带着孩子回来时，他立刻开始大吼大叫：

sentences.en: you can't keep yourself together, you can't do this, you can't do that.
sentences.zh: “你连自己都管不好，这个做不了，那个也做不了。”

sentences.en: Without steady employment and a husband to help with bills, Brandi watched anxiously as her household supplies dwindled.
sentences.zh: 由于没有稳定的工作，也没有丈夫分担账单，布兰迪焦虑地看着家里的物资一点点耗尽。

sentences.en: She worried constantly about money.
sentences.zh: 她时刻为钱发愁。

sentences.en: To make ends meet, she ordered a new credit card.
sentences.zh: 为了维持生计，她申请了一张新信用卡。

sentences.en: The day it arrived, Brandi tore open the envelope.
sentences.zh: 卡到那天，布兰迪撕开了信封。

sentences.en: She grabbed the card and ran out the door.
sentences.zh: 她抓起卡就跑出了门。

sentences.en: I went straight to Walmart, and I bought, like, a family size of toilet paper, family size of laundry detergent.
sentences.zh: 我直接去了沃尔玛，买了家庭装的卫生纸、家庭装的洗衣液。

sentences.en: Like, I stocked up on things all at once, rather than keeping it handy just in case.
sentences.zh: 我是一次性囤够了东西，而不是随用随买以备不时之需。

sentences.en: So I, like, maxed it out within the first couple of days that I had it, rather than holding on to it for emergency purposes.
sentences.zh: 所以，我在拿到卡的前几天就把额度刷爆了，而不是把它留作应急用。

sentences.en: And in that moment, as she was maxing out the credit card on the household supplies she needed,
sentences.zh: 就在那一刻，当她为了购买急需的家庭用品而刷爆信用卡时，

sentences.en: Brandi forgot about things that were slightly less pressing.
sentences.zh: 布兰迪忘记了那些稍微没那么紧迫的事情。

sentences.en: What I didn't think about is, what about gas money?
sentences.zh: 我没考虑到的是，油钱怎么办？

sentences.en: I didn't consider what gas would coSt.
sentences.zh: 我没考虑油费会是多少。

sentences.en: That was, like, the biggest thing.
sentences.zh: 那才是最大的问题。

sentences.en: It was always hard to have gas.
sentences.zh: 加油总是很困难。

sentences.en: And, of course, there was the credit card bill itself.
sentences.zh: 当然，还有信用卡账单本身。

sentences.en: The first two months, I paid the minimum payment, and then I just stopped paying, because I couldn't afford to pay.
sentences.zh: 前两个月我付了最低还款额，后来就干脆不付了，因为我实在付不起。

sentences.en: I didn't pay that card off until I got my tax refund the following year.
sentences.zh: 直到第二年拿到退税，我才还清那张卡。

sentences.en: By the time I paid it off, it was over $800 for a $500 card.
sentences.zh: 等我还清时，500美元的额度，最后还了800多美元。

sentences.en: More and more, Brandi felt trapped by debt.
sentences.zh: 布兰迪越来越感到被债务困住。

sentences.en: She no longer had options.
sentences.zh: 她已经没有选择了。

sentences.en: It came down to pay the bills or feed the kids.
sentences.zh: 归根结底，要么付账单，要么给孩子买吃的。

sentences.en: It was just overwhelming trying to juggle all of those things and still maintain a certain state of mind so that my children wouldn't see me struggle.
sentences.zh: 要兼顾所有这些事情，同时还要保持某种心态，不让孩子们看到我的挣扎，这简直让人崩溃。

sentences.en: In retrospect, Brandi can see the mistakes she made.
sentences.zh: 回过头看，布兰迪能看出自己犯的错误。

sentences.en: If she had made a budget for the whole month, she might have remembered she needed to account for gas.
sentences.zh: 如果她为整个月做了预算，她或许会记得要把油费算进去。

sentences.en: If she had focused on the big picture, she might not have maxed out a credit card she couldn't afford to pay back.
sentences.zh: 如果她关注大局，她或许就不会刷爆一张她根本还不起的信用卡。

sentences.en: Why did Brandi make these mistakes?
sentences.zh: 为什么布兰迪会犯这些错误？

sentences.en: It's easy to say she was being irresponsible.
sentences.zh: 说她不负责任很容易。

sentences.en: But here's the thing.
sentences.zh: 但问题在于：

sentences.en: She had always been careful and conscientious.
sentences.zh: 她一直以来都是个细心且认真的人。

sentences.en: Did something cause her to behave differently?
sentences.zh: 是什么导致她表现得如此反常？

sentences.en: When you have scarcity and it creates a scarcity mindset, it leads you to take certain behaviors which, in the short term, help you manage scarcity, but in the long term,
sentences.zh: 当你陷入稀缺状态并产生“稀缺心态”时，它会引导你采取某些行为，这些行为在短期内有助于你应对稀缺，但从长远来看，

sentences.en: only make matters worse.
sentences.zh: 只会让事情变得更糟。

sentences.en: When we come back, how the scarcity trap changes the way we think.
sentences.zh: 稍后回来，我们将探讨稀缺陷阱如何改变我们的思维方式。

sentences.en: Stay with us.
sentences.zh: 请继续收听。

sentences.en: After she lost her job, Brandi fell deeper and deeper into debt.
sentences.zh: 失业后，布兰迪陷入了越来越深的债务中。

sentences.en: One big reason is that she made a series of decisions that improved her life in the moment, but made it worse in the long run.
sentences.zh: 一个主要原因是，她做出了一系列决策，这些决策在当下改善了她的生活，但从长远来看却让情况恶化了。

sentences.en: She could have used the new credit card only for emergencies, but instead, she maxed it out in a couple of days.
sentences.zh: 她本可以只在紧急情况下使用那张新信用卡，但她却在几天内就把它刷爆了。

sentences.en: To understand why she did this, I want to take you to a completely different time and place,
sentences.zh: 为了理解她为什么这样做，我想带你去一个完全不同的时间和地点，

sentences.en: because it reveals something important about Brandi's story.
sentences.zh: 因为它揭示了关于布兰迪故事的重要信息。

sentences.en: World War II is nearing its end.
sentences.zh: 第二次世界大战即将结束。

sentences.en: Europe is on the verge of mass famine.
sentences.zh: 欧洲处于大规模饥荒的边缘。

sentences.en: Aid workers desperately need guidance on how to bring people back from the brink of starvation.
sentences.zh: 救援人员迫切需要指导，以了解如何将人们从饥饿的边缘拉回来。

sentences.en: Researchers at the University of Minnesota thought they could help.
sentences.zh: 明尼苏达大学的研究人员认为他们可以提供帮助。

sentences.en: They launched a year-long experiment.
sentences.zh: 他们发起了一项为期一年的实验。

sentences.en: As a 2002 documentary made by the university explains,
sentences.zh: 正如该大学在2002年制作的一部纪录片所解释的那样，

sentences.en: the volunteers were conscientious objectors who still wanted to serve their country.
sentences.zh: 志愿者们是那些仍想为国效力但拒绝服兵役的人。

sentences.en: The experiment?
sentences.zh: 实验内容是什么？

sentences.en: The volunteers had to go on a starvation diet.
sentences.zh: 志愿者们必须进行饥饿饮食。

sentences.en: Thirty-six young men, most of them Quakers, Mennonites, or Church of Brethren members,
sentences.zh: 36名年轻人，大多数是贵格会教徒、门诺派教徒或弟兄会成员，

sentences.en: moved into the South Tower of the Memorial Stadium, which would be their home for a year.
sentences.zh: 搬进了纪念体育场的南塔，那里将成为他们一年的家。

sentences.en: Many took courses at the university, even as they grew thinner and thinner.
sentences.zh: 许多人即使在变得越来越瘦的情况下，仍在大学里修读课程。

sentences.en: The young men became walking scarecrows.
sentences.zh: 这些年轻人变成了行走的稻草人。

sentences.en: Some grew so weak and bony, they couldn't sit without cushions or raise their arms to wash their hair.
sentences.zh: 有些人变得虚弱且骨瘦如柴，以至于没有垫子就坐不住，或者抬不起手臂来洗头。

sentences.en: I remember being a little bit critical of guys in the early part who would lick their plates.
sentences.zh: 我记得在实验初期，我还对那些舔盘子的人有些微词。

sentences.en: I thought that was really pretty crude.
sentences.zh: 我觉得那真的很粗鲁。

sentences.en: Henry Scholberg was one of the volunteers.
sentences.zh: 亨利·肖尔伯格是志愿者之一。

sentences.en: He recalled the experience in the documentary.
sentences.zh: 他在纪录片中回忆了这段经历。

sentences.en: By the time we were into about the second month of it, I was doing it myself.
sentences.zh: 到了第二个月左右，我自己也开始那样做了。

sentences.en: You just needed every single calorie you could get your hand on.
sentences.zh: 你只是需要你能弄到的每一卡路里。

sentences.en: The results of the starvation experiment were eventually published and remain an important academic reference
sentences.zh: 饥饿实验的结果最终被发表，并成为重要的学术参考，

sentences.en: on nutrition, famine, and eating disorders.
sentences.zh: 涉及营养学、饥荒和饮食失调等领域。

sentences.en: But recently, two researchers became intrigued with the 70-year-old study for a completely different reason.
sentences.zh: 但最近，两位研究人员出于完全不同的原因对这项70年前的研究产生了兴趣。

sentences.en: They were interested in what the lack of food did, not to the body, but to the mind.
sentences.zh: 他们感兴趣的是食物匮乏对人的影响，不是对身体，而是对大脑。

sentences.en: I think this type of scarcity is almost like an alarm that goes off in the head that's saying,
sentences.zh: 我认为这种稀缺就像大脑中响起的一个警报，它在说：

sentences.en: hey, we really need this thing addressed.
sentences.zh: “嘿，我们真的需要解决这个问题。”

sentences.en: We really need this thing addressed.
sentences.zh: “我们真的需要解决这个问题。”

sentences.en: This is Sendhil Moulayanathan, a professor of computation and behavioral science at the University of Chicago.
sentences.zh: 这是芝加哥大学计算与行为科学教授森德希尔·穆莱纳森。

sentences.en: He and a colleague, Eldar Shafir, a psychology professor at Princeton, had a theory brewing.
sentences.zh: 他和普林斯顿大学心理学教授埃尔达·沙菲尔当时正在酝酿一个理论。

sentences.en: It went like this.
sentences.zh: 理论是这样的：

sentences.en: When you feel that something important is missing in your life, your brain starts to focus on that missing thing.
sentences.zh: 当你感到生活中缺少某种重要的东西时，你的大脑就会开始专注于那个缺失的东西。

sentences.en: When you're really desperate for something, you can focus on it so obsessively, there's no room for anything else.
sentences.zh: 当你极度渴望某样东西时，你会痴迷地专注于它，以至于没有空间容纳其他任何东西。

sentences.en: The researchers were just beginning to explore their hypothesis when a colleague mentioned the long-ago Minnesota starvation experiment.
sentences.zh: 研究人员刚开始探索他们的假设时，一位同事提到了很久以前的明尼苏达饥饿实验。

sentences.en: Eldar remembers being immediately fascinated by the study and how the lack of food affected the minds of the men.
sentences.zh: 埃尔达记得自己立刻被这项研究迷住了，以及食物匮乏如何影响了那些人的思想。

sentences.en: They basically were very hungry and couldn't stop thinking about eating.
sentences.zh: 他们基本上是非常饥饿，满脑子想的都是吃。

sentences.en: In some sense, you would think, given that they cannot eat, they'd rather be distracted with other things.
sentences.zh: 从某种意义上说，你可能会认为，既然他们吃不到东西，他们宁愿被其他事情分散注意力。

sentences.en: But in fact, both subconsciously, the level of immediate reaction and their choice of conversation largely was around food.
sentences.zh: 但事实上，无论是潜意识里的即时反应，还是他们的谈话选择，很大程度上都围绕着食物。

sentences.en: It actually was sort of tragicomic.
sentences.zh: 这实际上有点悲喜交加。

sentences.en: I mean, they planned to open restaurants, to become restaurateurs.
sentences.zh: 我是说，他们计划开餐馆，想成为餐馆老板。

sentences.en: They memorized recipes.
sentences.zh: 他们背诵食谱。

sentences.en: They compared food prices at different newspapers.
sentences.zh: 他们比较不同报纸上的食品价格。

sentences.en: That's what they were doing.
sentences.zh: 这就是他们当时在做的事情。

sentences.en: The whole time, they sat around looking at food-related issues.
sentences.zh: 他们整天坐在一起讨论与食物相关的话题。

sentences.en: Even intentional diversions didn't work.
sentences.zh: 即使是刻意的转移注意力也不起作用。

sentences.en: Hunger and food had captured their minds.
sentences.zh: 饥饿和食物已经占据了他们的思想。

sentences.en: At some point, the experimenters just felt sorry for them and decided to distract them with a movie.
sentences.zh: 在某个时刻，实验者们只是对他们感到同情，决定用电影来分散他们的注意力。

sentences.en: And some of the testimonials were, they showed me this movie.
sentences.zh: 一些证词是这样的：他们给我看了这部电影。

sentences.en: I couldn't care less about the love scenes.
sentences.zh: 我根本不在乎爱情戏。

sentences.en: I wanted to see the meals.
sentences.zh: 我只想看里面的饭菜。

sentences.en: Eldar suddenly realized he had seen the same kind of behavior in a completely different setting.
sentences.zh: 埃尔达突然意识到，他在一个完全不同的环境中见过同样的行为。

sentences.en: He'd done a lot of research on the effects of poverty,
sentences.zh: 他曾对贫困的影响做过大量研究，

sentences.en: and he knew poor people who sometimes behaved like the starving men in Minnesota.
sentences.zh: 他认识一些穷人，他们的行为有时就像明尼苏达那些饥饿的人一样。

sentences.en: The poor, people who were lacking financial resources, found it very hard to think about anything but money,
sentences.zh: 穷人，那些缺乏经济资源的人，发现除了钱，他们很难思考其他任何事情。

sentences.en: or at least spend a lot of their cognitive resources, a lot of their attention, on financial juggling.
sentences.zh: 或者至少把大量的认知资源和注意力花在财务周转上。

sentences.en: If starvation made people obsess over food, poverty made people obsess over how they were going to make ends meet,
sentences.zh: 如果饥饿让人对食物产生执念，那么贫困就让人对如何维持生计产生执念，

sentences.en: how to make it to next week.
sentences.zh: 如何熬到下周。

sentences.en: What's in common in both cases is that your head is busy with a thing you don't have enough of.
sentences.zh: 这两种情况的共同点在于，你的大脑被你匮乏的东西占据了。

sentences.en: The two researchers felt they were on to something.
sentences.zh: 两位研究人员觉得他们发现了什么。

sentences.en: Maybe, they thought, the human brain is wired to respond to scarcity by tunneling in on the thing that's missing.
sentences.zh: 他们认为，也许人类大脑的运作机制就是通过聚焦于缺失的事物来应对匮乏。

sentences.en: Sendhil says this makes sense from an evolutionary perspective.
sentences.zh: 森德希尔说，从进化角度来看，这很有道理。

sentences.en: Picture that you have somebody from 25,000 years ago who's basically a hunter-gatherer
sentences.zh: 想象一下，25000年前的一个人，他基本上是个狩猎采集者，

sentences.en: and who might need to do a variety of things, such as, you know, get water, do a, you know, a lot of resources are needed.
sentences.zh: 他可能需要做各种各样的事情，比如，你知道，取水，做，你知道，需要很多资源。

sentences.en: When they get hungry, the sort of the evolutionary system wants to have an alarm that says,
sentences.zh: 当他们感到饥饿时，进化系统会发出一种警报，说：

sentences.en: hey, really focus on getting food into the system.
sentences.zh: 嘿，一定要专注于获取食物。

sentences.en: And that, I think, is the basic scarcity instinct.
sentences.zh: 我想，这就是基本的匮乏本能。

sentences.en: We're hungry.
sentences.zh: 我们饿了。

sentences.en: And then this thing starts going off in the head saying, do you realize we're hungry?
sentences.zh: 然后大脑里就开始响起警报，说：你意识到我们饿了吗？

sentences.en: Have I mentioned we're hungry?
sentences.zh: 我提过我们饿了吗？

sentences.en: We're hungry.
sentences.zh: 我们饿了。

sentences.en: And it just keeps calling out to you.
sentences.zh: 它就这样一直呼唤着你。

sentences.en: For Brandy Drew, the alarm might have sounded like this.
sentences.zh: 对于布兰迪·德鲁来说，警报声可能是这样的。

sentences.en: You don't have the necessities your family needs.
sentences.zh: 你没有家庭所需的必需品。

sentences.en: You need to stock up.
sentences.zh: 你需要囤货。

sentences.en: Stock up now.
sentences.zh: 现在就囤货。

sentences.en: You need these things.
sentences.zh: 你需要这些东西。

sentences.en: And when she bought the bleach, the family-sized pack of toilet paper, the snacks and juice boxes for the kids,
sentences.zh: 当她买了漂白剂、家庭装卫生纸、给孩子们的零食和果汁盒时，

sentences.en: the alarm temporarily went silent.
sentences.zh: 警报暂时安静了下来。

sentences.en: I felt relieved that those things, the small things, I didn't have to worry about.
sentences.zh: 我感到如释重负，那些小事，我不用再操心了。

sentences.en: But the reprieve from the alarm came at a huge coSt.
sentences.zh: 但这种警报的暂时平息付出了巨大的代价。

sentences.en: But then, like I said, two days later, it's like, okay, wait a minute.
sentences.zh: 但正如我所说，两天后，感觉就像是，好吧，等一下。

sentences.en: Why didn't you save at least $100 for gas?
sentences.zh: 为什么你没省下至少100美元来加油？

sentences.en: The answer to that question, Sendhil and Eldar believe, has to do with what scarcity did to Brandy.
sentences.zh: 森德希尔和埃尔达认为，这个问题的答案与匮乏对布兰迪的影响有关。

sentences.en: She was so focused on getting the basic necessities that she didn't have the mental capacity to attend to anything else.
sentences.zh: 她太专注于获取基本必需品，以至于没有足够的心理容量去关注其他任何事情。

sentences.en: There's a technical term for this.
sentences.zh: 这有一个专业术语。

sentences.en: It's called bandwidth.
sentences.zh: 它被称为带宽。

sentences.en: If you're downloading a movie on your home Wi-Fi network, you might find your email runs a little slower.
sentences.zh: 如果你在家庭Wi-Fi网络上下载电影，你可能会发现电子邮件运行得慢了一些。

sentences.en: The movie is hogging all the available bandwidth.
sentences.zh: 电影占用了所有可用的带宽。

sentences.en: Sendhil and Eldar say our minds work exactly the same way.
sentences.zh: 森德希尔和埃尔达说，我们的大脑运作方式完全一样。

sentences.en: If your mind is consumed with thoughts about something, there isn't room to think about other stuff.
sentences.zh: 如果你的大脑被某件事占据，就没有空间去思考其他事情了。

sentences.en: Scarcity fills the mind with intrusive thoughts about what you do not have.
sentences.zh: 匮乏让大脑充满了关于你所缺失事物的侵入性想法。

sentences.en: It doesn't leave room for anything else.
sentences.zh: 它没有留下任何空间给其他事情。

sentences.en: Eldar says there's a simple way to demonstrate this.
sentences.zh: 埃尔达说，有一个简单的方法可以证明这一点。

sentences.en: Imagine trying to hold an eight-digit number in your head.
sentences.zh: 想象一下，试着在脑子里记住一个八位数。

sentences.en: And if I simply ask you to keep in mind, you know, 26717164, that just leaves you less able to attend to other stuff.
sentences.zh: 如果我只是让你记住，你知道，26717164，这只会让你更难关注其他事情。

sentences.en: You'll eat less well.
sentences.zh: 你吃得不会那么好。

sentences.en: You'll pay attention to less things, et cetera.
sentences.zh: 你会关注更少的事情，等等。

sentences.en: As you're saying that eight-digit now and now, I didn't hear the rest of the next two sentences because I'm trying to remember that eight-digit number.
sentences.zh: 当你现在说那个八位数时，我没听清后面两句话的其余部分，因为我在努力记住那个八位数。

sentences.en: I won't test you.
sentences.zh: 我不会考你的。

sentences.en: I won't test you, I promise.
sentences.zh: 我不会考你的，我保证。

sentences.en: But in a sense, that's kind of the metaphor.
sentences.zh: 但在某种意义上，这算是一种隐喻。

sentences.en: So when you're busy juggling your resources, worrying about, you know, how am I going to pay for dinner?
sentences.zh: 所以当你忙于周转资源，担心，你知道，我该怎么付晚餐钱？

sentences.en: And if I pay for dinner, will I be able to have money for the kids' school trip?
sentences.zh: 如果我付了晚餐钱，我还能有钱给孩子们付学校旅行的费用吗？

sentences.en: It's that keeping an eight-digit number in your head.
sentences.zh: 这就像在脑子里记着一个八位数。

sentences.en: There's a reason our minds work this way.
sentences.zh: 我们的大脑这样运作是有原因的。

sentences.en: Tunneling into something makes you focus on it.
sentences.zh: 钻进隧道会让你专注于它。

sentences.en: Everything inside the tunnel becomes crystal clear.
sentences.zh: 隧道里的一切都变得清晰可见。

sentences.en: The problem is you can't see anything outside the tunnel.
sentences.zh: 问题是你看不见隧道外面的任何东西。

sentences.en: People in the poverty tunnel are actually very good at figuring out how to stretch the money they have to make it to tomorrow or the next week.
sentences.zh: 处于贫困隧道中的人实际上非常擅长计算如何利用现有的钱熬到明天或下周。

sentences.en: Studies show that the poor tend to be better than the rich at knowing where you can find the best deals, the cheap tube of toothpaste.
sentences.zh: 研究表明，穷人往往比富人更擅长寻找最划算的交易，比如便宜的牙膏。

sentences.en: Someone who is poor is often consumed with finding solutions to immediate probleMs.
sentences.zh: 穷人往往被寻找眼前问题的解决方案所消耗。

sentences.en: How do I get food on the table today?
sentences.zh: 我今天怎么才能让餐桌上有食物？

sentences.en: I'm not thinking about problems that are a few weeks away, like the utility bill or gas money or a credit card payment.
sentences.zh: 我没在想几周后的问题，比如水电费、油钱或信用卡账单。

sentences.en: As you're checking the prices and remembering the prices and figuring out if you buy two carats, will you have enough money for breakfast?
sentences.zh: 当你核对价格、记住价格并计算如果你买两个胡萝卜，你是否有足够的钱吃早餐时，

sentences.en: You are forgetting things.
sentences.zh: 你在遗忘其他事情。

sentences.en: You're paying less attention to your rent, to your kids' homework, to all the other things that make, you know, life complete.
sentences.zh: 你对房租、孩子的作业以及所有其他让生活完整的事情关注得更少了。

sentences.en: The thing is, as a result of doing this, the underlying problem can become worse.
sentences.zh: 问题是，由于这样做，潜在的问题可能会变得更糟。

sentences.en: If you don't pay your bills, you'll be even deeper in the hole next month.
sentences.zh: 如果你不付账单，下个月你会陷得更深。

sentences.en: Scarcity, in other words, is a trap.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，匮乏是一个陷阱。

sentences.en: The scarcity trap for us is all those ways in which scarcity today begets behaviors, which leads to even further scarcity tomorrow.
sentences.zh: 对我们来说，匮乏陷阱就是今天的匮乏导致了某些行为，从而导致明天的进一步匮乏。

sentences.en: And we think it's something that poor people do, busy people do.
sentences.zh: 我们认为这是穷人、忙碌的人才会做的事。

sentences.en: Here's another example.
sentences.zh: 这是另一个例子。

sentences.en: We think the lonely do this.
sentences.zh: 我们认为孤独的人也会这样。

sentences.en: So people who are lonely will often engage in social interactions in a particular way, which actually makes it harder for them to make friends.
sentences.zh: 所以孤独的人通常会以特定的方式进行社交互动，这实际上使他们更难交到朋友。

sentences.en: Just as the poor focus on the money they do not have, the lonely tend to focus on the friends they do not have.
sentences.zh: 就像穷人关注他们没有的钱一样，孤独的人往往关注他们没有的朋友。

sentences.en: The result is they try too hard to be liked.
sentences.zh: 结果就是他们太想讨人喜欢了。

sentences.en: In a conversation, the lonely person might be so preoccupied with making a good impression that he can't pay attention to what's actually being said.
sentences.zh: 在谈话中，孤独的人可能太专注于给人留下好印象，以至于无法注意对方实际在说什么。

sentences.en: The conversation falters.
sentences.zh: 谈话变得不顺畅。

sentences.en: Instead of appearing likable, he's seen as awkward or flat-footed.
sentences.zh: 他看起来不仅不讨人喜欢，反而显得笨拙或迟钝。

sentences.en: What happens as a result?
sentences.zh: 结果会怎样呢？

sentences.en: People avoid the awkward conversationaliSt.
sentences.zh: 人们避开这个笨拙的谈话者。

sentences.en: And the lonely person becomes even lonelier.
sentences.zh: 于是孤独的人变得更加孤独。

sentences.en: This lens offers a new way of thinking about why people who find themselves in scarcity seem to do things that, to an outsider, look stupid.
sentences.zh: 这个视角提供了一种新的思考方式，解释了为什么那些陷入匮乏的人在旁观者看来似乎在做蠢事。

sentences.en: When you're in a hole, why would you dig yourself even deeper?
sentences.zh: 当你身处困境时，为什么还要让自己陷得更深？

sentences.en: Sendhil says we're asking the wrong question.
sentences.zh: 森德希尔说我们问错了问题。

sentences.en: What if it's not the poor people are somehow deficient, but the poverty makes everyone less capable?
sentences.zh: 如果不是穷人有什么缺陷，而是贫困让每个人都变得能力不足呢？

sentences.en: That it's you and I tomorrow, were we to become poor, would all of a sudden have the same effect.
sentences.zh: 如果换作你我，明天如果我们变穷了，也会突然产生同样的效果。

sentences.en: That poverty is in some sense changing our minds.
sentences.zh: 贫困在某种意义上正在改变我们的大脑。

sentences.en: How do we know this isn't some bleeding-heart theory to excuse irresponsible behavior?
sentences.zh: 我们怎么知道这不是某种为了给不负责任的行为找借口的滥情理论？

sentences.en: Eldar and Sendhil wanted to test their hypothesis.
sentences.zh: 埃尔达和森德希尔想要验证他们的假设。

sentences.en: If all this is true, one thing that ought to be true is the same person, when they're poor, should have very different cognitive capacity than when they're rich.
sentences.zh: 如果这一切都是真的，那么有一点应该是真的：同一个人，在贫穷时应该比富有时的认知能力有很大不同。

sentences.en: So how would we test that?
sentences.zh: 那么我们该如何验证呢？

sentences.en: Well, unfortunately, we don't have the kind of money to go around making poor people rich.
sentences.zh: 嗯，不幸的是，我们没有那么多钱去让穷人变富。

sentences.en: But sugarcane farmers actually create a natural experiment for us.
sentences.zh: 但甘蔗农实际上为我们创造了一个自然实验。

sentences.en: Yes, sugarcane farmers.
sentences.zh: 没错，甘蔗农。

sentences.en: Specifically, those in India who are paid only once a year, right after the harveSt.
sentences.zh: 具体来说，是印度那些一年只领一次工资的农民，就在收获之后。

sentences.en: The month after they get that income, they're pretty rich.
sentences.zh: 拿到收入后的那个月，他们相当富有。

sentences.en: But like anybody who gets a huge windfall all at once, the money gets spent a little too faSt.
sentences.zh: 但就像任何突然获得巨额意外之财的人一样，钱花得有点太快了。

sentences.en: And so by the end of the harvest cycle, they're relatively poor.
sentences.zh: 所以到收获周期的末尾，他们相对贫穷。

sentences.en: So now we have the same person a month before harvest, poor, and a month after harvest, well off.
sentences.zh: 所以现在我们有了同一个人，收获前一个月是穷人，收获后一个月是富人。

sentences.en: Again, you have the same group of people who are poor one moment and rich the next.
sentences.zh: 同样，你拥有同一群人，前一刻贫穷，后一刻富有。

sentences.en: Sendhil and Eldar tested the farmers on their long-term thinking when they had no money and when they had plenty of money.
sentences.zh: 森德希尔和埃尔达测试了这些农民在没钱和有钱时的长期思考能力。

sentences.en: The results were stunning.
sentences.zh: 结果令人震惊。

sentences.en: We found a huge difference.
sentences.zh: 我们发现了巨大的差异。

sentences.en: So we found that post-harvest, when they're well off, they have much more impulse control.
sentences.zh: 我们发现，收获后，当他们富裕时，他们的冲动控制能力要强得多。

sentences.en: Farmers who were rich tended to think about things that would help them over the long term.
sentences.zh: 富裕的农民倾向于考虑那些对长期有帮助的事情。

sentences.en: This matched other research that shows, for example, that farmers who are well off tend to weed their fields more regularly than farmers who are poor.
sentences.zh: 这与其他研究相吻合，例如，富裕的农民往往比贫穷的农民更定期地给田地除草。

sentences.en: Farmers who were poor mostly focused on how to make it to next week.
sentences.zh: 贫穷的农民大多专注于如何熬到下周。

sentences.en: Short-term thinking.
sentences.zh: 短期思考。

sentences.en: To be clear, it's not that poor people focus on immediate needs because that's all they want to think about.
sentences.zh: 需要明确的是，并不是穷人只关注眼前需求，因为他们只想考虑这些。

sentences.en: It's all they can think about.
sentences.zh: 而是他们只能考虑这些。

sentences.en: Scarcity captures the mind like it did with those starving men in Minnesota.
sentences.zh: 匮乏占据了大脑，就像明尼苏达州那些挨饿的人一样。

sentences.en: In fact, scarcity can actually lower how you perform on an IQ teSt.
sentences.zh: 事实上，匮乏实际上会降低你在智商测试中的表现。

sentences.en: Put simply, being poor is like having just pulled an all-nighter.
sentences.zh: 简单来说，贫穷就像刚熬了个通宵。

sentences.en: Now, if you've been very lucky, maybe you've never experienced what it's like to be poor or hungry or lonely.
sentences.zh: 现在，如果你很幸运，也许你从未经历过贫穷、饥饿或孤独的感觉。

sentences.en: But there might be another form of scarcity you have experienced.
sentences.zh: 但你可能经历过另一种形式的匮乏。

sentences.en: On some days we get to leave at 4 p.m., some days we don't leave till 1 a.m.
sentences.zh: 有些日子我们下午4点就能走，有些日子我们直到凌晨1点才离开。

sentences.en: And then you usually start the next day at 5.30 or 6 in the morning.
sentences.zh: 然后你通常在第二天早上5点半或6点就开始工作了。

sentences.en: Usually work 80 hours-ish a week.
sentences.zh: 通常每周工作80小时左右。

sentences.en: When we come back, how being overworked and exhausted can produce a form of scarcity too,
sentences.zh: 当我们回来时，会谈谈过度劳累和精疲力竭如何也会产生一种匮乏，

sentences.en: and the pernicious effect this can have on your life.
sentences.zh: 以及这对你的生活可能产生的有害影响。

sentences.en: Stay with us.
sentences.zh: 请继续关注我们。

sentences.en: Eldar Shafir and Sendhil Mulayanathan believe that when something you desperately need is in short supply,
sentences.zh: 埃尔达·沙菲尔和森德希尔·穆莱纳坦认为，当你迫切需要的东西供应不足时，

sentences.en: your brain tends to focus on that thing.
sentences.zh: 你的大脑往往会专注于那件事。

sentences.en: This focus can be so intense that it impedes your ability to think about anything else.
sentences.zh: 这种专注力可能非常强烈，以至于阻碍了你思考其他任何事情的能力。

sentences.en: What happens when the thing you're missing is time?
sentences.zh: 当你缺失的东西是时间时会发生什么？

sentences.en: When you're so busy, it feels like you don't have time to breathe.
sentences.zh: 当你太忙时，感觉就像没有时间呼吸。

sentences.en: Let me tell you the story of a young woman named Katie.
sentences.zh: 让我给你讲讲一个叫凯蒂的年轻女人的故事。

sentences.en: She asked us to use her middle name for reasons that will be clear in a moment.
sentences.zh: 她要求我们使用她的中间名，原因一会儿就会清楚。

sentences.en: For as long as she can remember, Katie has been driven.
sentences.zh: 在凯蒂的记忆中，她一直很有进取心。

sentences.en: Really driven.
sentences.zh: 非常有进取心。

sentences.en: When I was in high school, I was determined to be valedictorian,
sentences.zh: 我在高中时，就下定决心要成为毕业生代表，

sentences.en: so I took a sophomore-level honors biology course as a freshman in high school,
sentences.zh: 所以我在高一就修了大学二年级水平的荣誉生物课，

sentences.en: and I studied around the clock.
sentences.zh: 我没日没夜地学习。

sentences.en: I had note cards.
sentences.zh: 我有笔记卡片。

sentences.en: I walked through the hallways with the note cards.
sentences.zh: 我拿着笔记卡片走在走廊里。

sentences.en: If there was a holiday party, I brought the note cards.
sentences.zh: 如果有节日聚会，我就带着笔记卡片。

sentences.en: And I'd also study till 2 or 3 in the morning.
sentences.zh: 我还会学习到凌晨2点或3点。

sentences.en: Katie says she wanted to be perfect at school.
sentences.zh: 凯蒂说她想在学校里做到完美。

sentences.en: She eventually got to medical school, where she excelled.
sentences.zh: 她最终进入了医学院，在那里表现优异。

sentences.en: She graduated at the top of her class and quickly started her residency.
sentences.zh: 她以班级第一名的成绩毕业，并很快开始了住院医师实习。

sentences.en: The new schedule was grueling.
sentences.zh: 新的时间表非常折磨人。

sentences.en: You can get in at 5.30 or 6 in the morning, and you round on all your patients,
sentences.zh: 你可以在早上5点半或6点到达，查房所有的病人，

sentences.en: and then you round with the team.
sentences.zh: 然后和团队一起查房。

sentences.en: That means you go to all the patients and check in on their plan
sentences.zh: 这意味着你要去看所有的病人，核对他们的治疗计划，

sentences.en: and adjust medications, etc., as necessary.
sentences.zh: 并根据需要调整药物等。

sentences.en: And then there's usually a lunch conference where we have education,
sentences.zh: 然后通常会有午餐会议进行教育培训，

sentences.en: and then in the afternoon we might take new patients in and keep following up on our patients.
sentences.zh: 下午我们可能会接收新病人并继续跟进我们的病人。

sentences.en: And on some days we get to leave at 4 p.m., some days we don't leave till 1 a.m.
sentences.zh: 有些日子我们下午4点就能走，有些日子我们直到凌晨1点才离开。

sentences.en: So, and then you usually start the next day at 5.30 or 6 in the morning again.
sentences.zh: 所以，然后你通常在第二天早上5点半或6点又开始了。

sentences.en: And you get one day off a week.
sentences.zh: 你每周有一天的休息时间。

sentences.en: Usually work 80 hours-ish a week.
sentences.zh: 通常每周工作80小时左右。

sentences.en: As Katie's workload grew, she started to feel she couldn't afford to waste a single moment.
sentences.zh: 随着凯蒂的工作量增加，她开始觉得她浪费不起哪怕一刻钟。

sentences.en: Instead of spending any time relaxing,
sentences.zh: 而不是花时间放松，

sentences.en: she started to focus only on things directly related to her success at work.
sentences.zh: 她开始只关注那些与她工作成就直接相关的事情。

sentences.en: When I first started, it was just like really busy,
sentences.zh: 我刚开始的时候，真的非常忙，

sentences.en: so I'd try to come home and I felt like, you know,
sentences.zh: 所以我试着回家，但我感觉，你知道，

sentences.en: I just don't have a lot of hours, so I need to make the most of them.
sentences.zh: 我的时间实在太少了，所以我必须充分利用它们。

sentences.en: And I was like, okay, I need to make sure I'm exercising,
sentences.zh: 当时我想，好吧，我得确保自己有在锻炼，

sentences.en: keeping my body healthy, and I need to read and stay on top of things.
sentences.zh: 保持身体健康，我还得阅读，跟上进度。

sentences.en: So I'd come home after a pretty long day and I might go walking for half an hour
sentences.zh: 所以，在漫长的一天结束后，我会回家，可能会去散步半小时，

sentences.en: and then I'd read and then I'd go to sleep.
sentences.zh: 然后阅读，接着就去睡觉。

sentences.en: But then as the time went on, I decided to try to get in more exercise
sentences.zh: 但随着时间的推移，我决定尝试增加运动量，

sentences.en: because I'm like, I never know when I'll get enough exercise in.
sentences.zh: 因为我觉得，我永远不知道什么时候才能有足够的运动时间。

sentences.en: So I started spending all my free daylight hours walking or running outside
sentences.zh: 于是我开始把我所有白天的空闲时间都花在户外散步或跑步上，

sentences.en: or going to the gym up to three hours a day plus like working 15-hour days
sentences.zh: 或者每天去健身房锻炼长达三个小时，再加上每天15小时的工作，

sentences.en: and then trying to read and then go to sleep.
sentences.zh: 然后还要试着阅读，接着去睡觉。

sentences.en: As she focused intensely on the things she believed were key to her professional success,
sentences.zh: 由于凯蒂过度专注于她认为对职业成功至关重要的事情，

sentences.en: Katie lost sight of things on the periphery.
sentences.zh: 她忽略了周遭的其他事物。

sentences.en: She didn't know it, but she was entering the tunnel of scarcity.
sentences.zh: 她自己并不知道，她正在进入“稀缺”的隧道。

sentences.en: In her case, it was scarcity brought on by a lack of time.
sentences.zh: 就她而言，这种稀缺是由时间匮乏引起的。

sentences.en: So I wasn't going to the grocery store.
sentences.zh: 所以我没去杂货店买东西。

sentences.en: My house wasn't unpacked yet and it was stressing me out.
sentences.zh: 我的房子还没整理好，这让我感到压力很大。

sentences.en: It was just a mess and my clothes piled up.
sentences.zh: 家里乱七八糟，衣服堆积如山。

sentences.en: I had a lot of dirty clothes and coming home just felt so overwhelming.
sentences.zh: 我有很多脏衣服，回家让我感到无比压抑。

sentences.en: I didn't want to be there and that's part of, I think, why I was walking so much,
sentences.zh: 我不想待在那里，我想这也是我为什么走那么多路的原因之一，

sentences.en: just to get out of the house and get away from all the things I hadn't done.
sentences.zh: 只是为了离开家，逃避那些我还没做完的事情。

sentences.en: And I also forgot to pay a bill in the mix of all of this.
sentences.zh: 而且在这一团乱麻中，我还忘了付账单。

sentences.en: What did you forget to do?
sentences.zh: 你忘了做什么？

sentences.en: What bill did you forget to pay?
sentences.zh: 你忘了付什么账单？

sentences.en: It was my energy bill.
sentences.zh: 是我的电费账单。

sentences.en: The old Katie would have spotted all of this.
sentences.zh: 以前的凯蒂肯定会注意到这一切的。

sentences.en: I mean, you were just basically at this point almost falling apart, it sounds like.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，听起来你当时基本上快要崩溃了。

sentences.en: I was.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: I was falling apart.
sentences.zh: 我确实快崩溃了。

sentences.en: There was something else.
sentences.zh: 还有别的事。

sentences.en: Katie had battled anorexia as a teenager.
sentences.zh: 凯蒂青少年时期曾与厌食症抗争过。

sentences.en: She knew she had to stay vigilant about her eating.
sentences.zh: 她知道自己必须时刻警惕饮食问题。

sentences.en: But as she started to focus ever more intensely on work, she slipped back into some old habits.
sentences.zh: 但随着她开始更加专注于工作，她又陷入了一些旧习惯。

sentences.en: I was eating mostly vegetables and fruits and I wasn't eating a whole lot else, maybe a
sentences.zh: 我当时主要吃蔬菜和水果，几乎不吃别的，偶尔可能吃一根

sentences.en: Clif Bar here and there.
sentences.zh: Clif能量棒。

sentences.en: Despite all her medical training, Katie stopped taking care of herself.
sentences.zh: 尽管受过医学训练，凯蒂还是停止了照顾自己。

sentences.en: Here's one thing I haven't told you yet about scarcity.
sentences.zh: 关于稀缺，还有一点我还没告诉你。

sentences.en: It can rob you of insight.
sentences.zh: 它会剥夺你的洞察力。

sentences.en: Insight about how your own mind is changing.
sentences.zh: 关于你自己的思维正在如何改变的洞察力。

sentences.en: Katie had no awareness that she was heading down a dangerous path.
sentences.zh: 凯蒂完全没有意识到自己正在走向一条危险的道路。

sentences.en: It became obvious to her only when it finally affected her work.
sentences.zh: 直到它最终影响到她的工作，她才察觉到。

sentences.en: I started to notice that I was like nearly missing things as I was reviewing.
sentences.zh: 我开始注意到，我在复核时差点漏掉一些东西。

sentences.en: For example, I admitted a diabetic and I almost didn't order insulin for them.
sentences.zh: 例如，我收治了一名糖尿病患者，差点没给他们开胰岛素。

sentences.en: But I did order the insulin.
sentences.zh: 但我最终还是开了胰岛素。

sentences.en: But I was like, I don't think I can keep up with this anymore.
sentences.zh: 但我当时想，我觉得我再也无法应付这些了。

sentences.en: Because if you don't give a diabetic insulin, especially if they're type 1, they can have
sentences.zh: 因为如果你不给糖尿病患者注射胰岛素，尤其是1型糖尿病患者，他们可能会在医院里

sentences.en: very fatal circumstances in the hospital and get really high blood sugars that can cause
sentences.zh: 面临致命的情况，血糖过高可能导致

sentences.en: them to have an acidosis and end up on a ventilator.
sentences.zh: 他们出现酸中毒，最终需要使用呼吸机。

sentences.en: So I turned myself in at the point that I saw that it was starting to affect my work.
sentences.zh: 所以，当我发现它开始影响我的工作时，我主动坦白了。

sentences.en: In two months of the residency program, Katie's body and mind had withered.
sentences.zh: 在住院医师项目的两个月里，凯蒂的身心已经枯竭。

sentences.en: Things had gotten so bad, she had to go to a residential treatment center.
sentences.zh: 情况变得如此糟糕，她不得不去了一家住院治疗中心。

sentences.en: Katie struggled with two things.
sentences.zh: 凯蒂当时面临两个问题。

sentences.en: Her body was desperately in need of nutrition.
sentences.zh: 她的身体极度需要营养。

sentences.en: And her mind.
sentences.zh: 还有她的精神。

sentences.en: She had to find a way to stop the intrusive thoughts that were consuming her.
sentences.zh: 她必须找到一种方法来停止那些折磨她的侵入性思维。

sentences.en: She had to...
sentences.zh: 她必须……

sentences.en: Learn how to just sit.
sentences.zh: 学会如何静坐。

sentences.en: Because we weren't allowed to exercise.
sentences.zh: 因为我们不被允许运动。

sentences.en: We weren't allowed to stand.
sentences.zh: 我们不被允许站立。

sentences.en: We weren't even allowed to do jumping jacks or squats.
sentences.zh: 我们甚至不被允许做开合跳或深蹲。

sentences.en: We had to just sit.
sentences.zh: 我们只能坐着。

sentences.en: Katie's mind was filled with angry and impatient thoughts.
sentences.zh: 凯蒂的脑海里充满了愤怒和急躁的念头。

sentences.en: At first, I felt like I felt useless because I thought, you know, if I'm not doing something
sentences.zh: 起初，我感到自己很没用，因为我想，你知道，如果我不做点

sentences.en: productive, what is my purpose in life?
sentences.zh: 有成效的事，我活着的意义是什么？

sentences.en: But gradually, as the program literally forced her to do nothing, Katie started to emerge
sentences.zh: 但渐渐地，当项目强制她什么都不做时，凯蒂开始从

sentences.en: from the tunnel.
sentences.zh: 隧道中走出来。

sentences.en: She realized she had been so narrowly, relentlessly focused on one goal, doing well at work, that
sentences.zh: 她意识到自己之前一直狭隘而无情地专注于一个目标，即在工作中表现出色，以至于

sentences.en: she'd ignored the very things she needed to succeed.
sentences.zh: 她忽略了成功所必需的东西。

sentences.en: Moments of relaxation, like watching TV, or in her case, painting.
sentences.zh: 放松的时刻，比如看电视，或者对她来说，是绘画。

sentences.en: Katie had loved art as a child, but she had put it aside because she thought it wouldn't
sentences.zh: 凯蒂小时候很喜欢艺术，但她把它搁置了，因为她认为这不会

sentences.en: help her become a better doctor.
sentences.zh: 帮助她成为一名更好的医生。

sentences.en: I'm kind of the type of person that just likes to study and then do after I've, like, mastered
sentences.zh: 我属于那种喜欢先学习，然后在从学习的角度

sentences.en: it from a study point of view.
sentences.zh: 掌握它之后再去做的人。

sentences.en: And so to just do something without instruction is, it feels very vulnerable to me, but it
sentences.zh: 所以，在没有指导的情况下做某事，让我感到非常脆弱，但这

sentences.en: ended up kind of being my saving grace in my recovery.
sentences.zh: 最终成了我康复过程中的救命稻草。

sentences.en: And I've actually created an art room in my house.
sentences.zh: 我甚至在家里专门开辟了一个艺术室。

sentences.en: I changed my office from a workroom into an art room.
sentences.zh: 我把办公室从工作间改成了艺术室。

sentences.en: And it has paints and watercolors and chalks and everything you can imagine.
sentences.zh: 里面有颜料、水彩、粉笔，还有你能想象到的一切。

sentences.en: And I try to go in there once a week and just create something without any expectation
sentences.zh: 我试着每周进去一次，不带任何期望地创作点什么，

sentences.en: just for the purpose of creating it, because I can.
sentences.zh: 仅仅是为了创作而创作，因为我可以这样做。

sentences.en: Katie eventually returned to her residency program with a new outlook.
sentences.zh: 凯蒂最终以全新的视角回到了住院医师项目。

sentences.en: She started doing something that Eldar and Sendil recommend to all busy people.
sentences.zh: 她开始做一些埃尔达和森迪尔建议所有忙碌的人去做的事情。

sentences.en: She actually pencils time into her schedule to do nothing.
sentences.zh: 她真的在日程表里预留了什么都不做的时间。

sentences.en: One of the big things I've done is I kind of have a date night with myself once or twice
sentences.zh: 我做的一件大事就是，我每周会给自己安排一两次

sentences.en: a week, where I just schedule off the night and I won't do anything with anyone else.
sentences.zh: “约会之夜”，我会把那个晚上空出来，不和任何人做任何事。

sentences.en: And it'll just be free for me to do what I feel like.
sentences.zh: 那段时间我可以自由地做我想做的事。

sentences.en: It might be watching a movie.
sentences.zh: 可能是看部电影。

sentences.en: It might be taking a soak in the tub and reading a book or being in my art room and painting
sentences.zh: 可能是泡个澡读本书，或者待在艺术室里画画，

sentences.en: whatever comes to me.
sentences.zh: 画任何我想画的东西。

sentences.en: But I do, like, I prioritize that.
sentences.zh: 但我确实把这当作优先事项。

sentences.en: And I actually won't accept plans with friends generally when I do this.
sentences.zh: 通常情况下，我不会在做这件事时接受朋友的邀约。

sentences.en: So that's one of the things I do.
sentences.zh: 这就是我做的事情之一。

sentences.en: Katie is consciously freeing up bandwidth.
sentences.zh: 凯蒂正在有意识地释放带宽。

sentences.en: And something strange has happened as she's done so.
sentences.zh: 而在她这样做的时候，发生了一些奇怪的事情。

sentences.en: The less consumed she feels about work, the better she does at work.
sentences.zh: 她对工作感到越不执着，她在工作中的表现就越好。

sentences.en: Honestly, like, it's kind of incredible.
sentences.zh: 老实说，这简直不可思议。

sentences.en: But at work, my brain has increased its capacity fourfold.
sentences.zh: 但在工作中，我的大脑容量增加了四倍。

sentences.en: I am able to hold so many more things in my consciousness at once and manage them.
sentences.zh: 我能够同时在意识中处理更多的事情并管理它们。

sentences.en: I've just seen a really huge improvement in my ability to enjoy being in the company of
sentences.zh: 我发现自己在享受与他人相处、享受场合、享受工作以及在工作中表现出色方面的能力

sentences.en: others, to enjoy, like, occasions and to enjoy my work and do well at my work.
sentences.zh: 有了巨大的提升。

sentences.en: While the psychological studies into scarcity and bandwidth are relatively new,
sentences.zh: 虽然关于稀缺和带宽的心理学研究相对较新，

sentences.en: the ideas are actually ancient.
sentences.zh: 但这些理念其实古已有之。

sentences.en: Avoid tunnel vision.
sentences.zh: 避免隧道视野。

sentences.en: Keep difficult things in one part of your life from contaminating everything else.
sentences.zh: 不要让你生活中的困难部分影响到其他方面。

sentences.en: Be present.
sentences.zh: 活在当下。

sentences.en: Say you have a big deadline tomorrow for something you've got to finish.
sentences.zh: 假设你明天有一个必须完成的重要截止日期。

sentences.en: You go home and you're spending the evening with your kids.
sentences.zh: 你回到家，本该和孩子们共度夜晚。

sentences.en: And in that moment, you're not present-focused at all.
sentences.zh: 但在那一刻，你根本没有活在当下。

sentences.en: What you're focused on is that deadline.
sentences.zh: 你关注的是那个截止日期。

sentences.en: You may go through minutes where you didn't hear what your kids were saying to you
sentences.zh: 你可能会经历好几分钟，根本没听见孩子们在对你说什么，

sentences.en: because your mind keeps going to this other thing.
sentences.zh: 因为你的思绪一直飘向那件事。

sentences.en: Tunnel vision is not in itself a good thing or a bad thing.
sentences.zh: 隧道视野本身无所谓好坏。

sentences.en: Shutting out distractions can be helpful at times.
sentences.zh: 屏蔽干扰有时是有帮助的。

sentences.en: The question is, do you know when you're inside the tunnel?
sentences.zh: 问题是，你知道自己何时身处隧道中吗？

sentences.en: To me, that's exactly the heart of managing scarcity.
sentences.zh: 对我来说，这正是管理稀缺的核心。

sentences.en: It's recognizing when are you trying to do something related to your scarcity
sentences.zh: 关键在于识别你何时是在尝试处理与稀缺相关的事情，

sentences.en: where you really want to use that instinct.
sentences.zh: 并确实想要利用那种本能。

sentences.en: And when have you made a conscious decision to do something else
sentences.zh: 以及你何时做出了有意识的决定去做别的事情，

sentences.en: where what you really need to do is to not have it intrude on that something else.
sentences.zh: 而你真正需要做的是不让它干扰到那件别的事情。

sentences.en: You're at home.
sentences.zh: 你在家里。

sentences.en: You're with your kids.
sentences.zh: 你和孩子们在一起。

sentences.en: You chose to be a parent for that three-hour period.
sentences.zh: 你选择了在那三个小时里做一个父母。

sentences.en: You really don't want scarcity to intrude then.
sentences.zh: 你真的不希望稀缺在那时进行干扰。

sentences.en: Of course, it's easy to say, build free time into your schedule.
sentences.zh: 当然，说起来容易，在日程表里预留空闲时间。

sentences.en: Stay present with your family.
sentences.zh: 多陪陪家人。

sentences.en: Take a vacation.
sentences.zh: 去度假。

sentences.en: These strategies presume you have choices.
sentences.zh: 这些策略的前提是你拥有选择权。

sentences.en: You can't say, I've had it with being lonely.
sentences.zh: 你不能说，我受够了孤独。

sentences.en: I'm going to take a vacation from being lonely.
sentences.zh: 我要从孤独中休个假。

sentences.en: It's not a choice.
sentences.zh: 这不是一种选择。

sentences.en: And to me, loneliness and poverty are the forms of scarcity that feel the biggest
sentences.zh: 对我来说，孤独和贫困是感觉最沉重的稀缺形式，

sentences.en: because while all these forces are at play, there's no release valve.
sentences.zh: 因为当所有这些力量都在起作用时，根本没有释放阀。

sentences.en: There's no escape mechanism.
sentences.zh: 没有逃脱机制。

sentences.en: Eldar and Sendhil want policymakers to design solutions that recognize how scarcity creates traps
sentences.zh: 埃尔达和森迪尔希望政策制定者设计出的解决方案能认识到稀缺是如何制造陷阱的，

sentences.en: from which many people may not be able to extricate themselves.
sentences.zh: 许多人可能无法从中自拔。

sentences.en: And they want the rest of us to stop preaching to those in poverty.
sentences.zh: 他们也希望我们其他人停止对贫困人群说教。

sentences.en: If you look at programs of poverty, we often confound a little bit the attempt to help the poor
sentences.zh: 如果你看看扶贫项目，我们往往会把帮助穷人的尝试与教育他们混为一谈，

sentences.en: with the attempt to educate them, make sure that they show up in time, that they do the right things.
sentences.zh: 确保他们准时出现，确保他们做正确的事。

sentences.en: From the perspective we're taking with scarcity, in some sense,
sentences.zh: 从我们看待稀缺的视角来看，在某种意义上，

sentences.en: if I'm very busy juggling a very complicated life, insisting that I show up at the office at 8
sentences.zh: 如果我正忙于应付复杂的生活，坚持要求我8点准时出现在办公室，

sentences.en: and not 8.05, it's not doing me a favor.
sentences.zh: 而不是8点05分，这对我来说并没有什么帮助。

sentences.en: I don't need to be educated.
sentences.zh: 我不需要被教育。

sentences.en: It's just hard to manage.
sentences.zh: 这只是很难管理而已。

sentences.en: You know, the transportation is not reliable.
sentences.zh: 你知道，交通不靠谱。

sentences.en: My kid is not ready.
sentences.zh: 我的孩子还没准备好。

sentences.en: I don't have a babysitter.
sentences.zh: 我没有保姆。

sentences.en: I'm going to make mistakes that it's not clear educating me, in quotes, about them is going to help me at all.
sentences.zh: 我会犯错，而“教育”我这些错误根本帮不了我什么。

sentences.en: It just makes my life all the more complicated.
sentences.zh: 这只会让我的生活变得更加复杂。

sentences.en: When people in poverty fail or make mistakes, the researchers think we should respond to them
sentences.zh: 当贫困人群遭遇失败或犯错时，研究人员认为我们应该以对待

sentences.en: the same way we respond to mistakes made by airline pilots.
sentences.zh: 飞行员犯错时同样的方式来应对。

sentences.en: There was a time not long ago when we thought that airline pilots who made mistakes were just bad pilots.
sentences.zh: 曾几何时，我们还认为犯错的飞行员仅仅是糟糕的飞行员。

sentences.en: Sendhil says a big reason air travel has become safer in recent decades
sentences.zh: 森迪尔说，近几十年来航空旅行变得更加安全的一个重要原因

sentences.en: is that there has been a shift in thinking about such mistakes.
sentences.zh: 在于人们对这类错误的看法发生了转变。

sentences.en: Designers have made cockpits fault-tolerant.
sentences.zh: 设计师们让驾驶舱具备了容错能力。

sentences.en: Rather than trying to find perfect pilots,
sentences.zh: 与其试图寻找完美的飞行员，

sentences.en: cockpits are now designed to account for human error.
sentences.zh: 现在的驾驶舱设计已经考虑到了人为失误。

sentences.en: The goal is to alert pilots when they've made a mistake
sentences.zh: 其目标是在飞行员犯错时发出警报，

sentences.en: and to diminish the consequences of mistakes.
sentences.zh: 并减少错误带来的后果。

sentences.en: It's ironic that when we design cockpits,
sentences.zh: 讽刺的是，当我们设计驾驶舱时，

sentences.en: the entire mantra of fault-tolerance seems so intuitive.
sentences.zh: 容错这一核心准则显得如此直观。

sentences.en: But when we design social policies,
sentences.zh: 但当我们设计社会政策时，

sentences.en: nobody's out there talking about,
sentences.zh: 却没人会去谈论，

sentences.en: let's make this fault-tolerant.
sentences.zh: 让我们把这个政策设计得具备容错性吧。

sentences.en: I mean, you know, poor people have a lot on their mind.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，你知道，穷人要操心的事情太多了。

sentences.en: Their bandwidth is taxed.
sentences.zh: 他们的心智带宽被占满了。

sentences.en: They're going to make mistakes.
sentences.zh: 他们难免会犯错。

sentences.en: Let's make sure this program is robust when they do make that mistake.
sentences.zh: 我们应该确保当他们犯错时，这个项目依然稳健有效。

sentences.en: It's just not the way we think.
sentences.zh: 但这根本不是我们的思考方式。

sentences.en: If I offer a training program,
sentences.zh: 如果我提供一个培训项目，

sentences.en: I don't sit there and say,
sentences.zh: 我不会坐在那儿想，

sentences.en: let me make sure, you know what's going to happen?
sentences.zh: 让我确认一下，你知道会发生什么吗？

sentences.en: This is for low-income individuals.
sentences.zh: 这是为低收入群体准备的。

sentences.en: Surely they're going to miss a few days
sentences.zh: 他们肯定会缺席几天，

sentences.en: because, you know, it's hard to get to class sometimes
sentences.zh: 因为，你知道，有时候很难赶去上课，

sentences.en: or other things are on their mind.
sentences.zh: 或者他们还有其他心事。

sentences.en: So let me design this curriculum
sentences.zh: 所以我应该设计好这个课程，

sentences.en: so that it's in attendance tolerant.
sentences.zh: 让它具备出勤容错性。

sentences.en: So even if somebody misses three days in a row,
sentences.zh: 这样即使有人连续缺席三天，

sentences.en: you'll be able to come on that fourth day
sentences.zh: 第四天来上课时，

sentences.en: and still feel caught up.
sentences.zh: 依然能跟上进度。

sentences.en: In fact, a training curriculum is often quite the opposite.
sentences.zh: 事实上，培训课程往往恰恰相反。

sentences.en: If you miss three days in a row,
sentences.zh: 如果你连续缺席三天，

sentences.en: it's an invitation to miss the fourth day
sentences.zh: 那简直就是让你第四天也别来了，

sentences.en: because you're not going to get anything.
sentences.zh: 因为你根本听不懂了。

sentences.en: Brandi Drew eventually turned her life around.
sentences.zh: 布兰迪·德鲁最终扭转了她的人生。

sentences.en: She found a low-income assistance program
sentences.zh: 她找到了一个低收入援助项目，

sentences.en: that offered her help.
sentences.zh: 并获得了帮助。

sentences.en: She worked with a financial counselor
sentences.zh: 她与一位财务顾问合作，

sentences.en: who gave her strategies for budgeting her money
sentences.zh: 对方为她提供了预算管理策略，

sentences.en: and keeping track of long-term priorities.
sentences.zh: 并让她学会关注长期的优先事项。

sentences.en: I actually have a calendar now that I write down everything
sentences.zh: 我现在确实有一个日历，我会把所有事情都写下来，

sentences.en: to make sure I'm paying things on the correct day and time.
sentences.zh: 以确保我在正确的时间和日期支付账单。

sentences.en: It's taken time and little steps,
sentences.zh: 这需要时间和一点一滴的努力，

sentences.en: but Brandi is no longer in the scarcity tunnel.
sentences.zh: 但布兰迪已经不再处于稀缺心态的隧道视野中了。

sentences.en: She's been working for two years now,
sentences.zh: 她已经工作两年了，

sentences.en: and she has savings.
sentences.zh: 而且有了积蓄。

sentences.en: I know that if anything happens,
sentences.zh: 我知道如果发生什么事，

sentences.en: God forbid, if I lose this job,
sentences.zh: 哪怕是天灾人祸，如果我丢了这份工作，

sentences.en: I know that I can survive for at least six months
sentences.zh: 我知道我至少能维持六个月的生活，

sentences.en: if I have to look for another.
sentences.zh: 足够我去找下一份工作。

sentences.en: Eldar and Sendhil themselves say
sentences.zh: 埃尔达和森迪尔本人也说，

sentences.en: they are constantly trying to keep the lessons of scarcity
sentences.zh: 他们一直在努力将稀缺性的教训，

sentences.en: front and center in their own lives.
sentences.zh: 放在自己生活的核心位置。

sentences.en: As a busy academic, Eldar has come up with a rule.
sentences.zh: 作为一名忙碌的学者，埃尔达想出了一个规则。

sentences.en: When an invitation to an event two months down the road comes along,
sentences.zh: 当收到两个月后的活动邀请时，

sentences.en: he asks himself whether he would attend the event
sentences.zh: 他会问自己，如果这个活动是明天举行，

sentences.en: if it were tomorrow.
sentences.zh: 他还会参加吗？

sentences.en: If the answer is no, he declines the invitation
sentences.zh: 如果答案是否定的，他就会拒绝邀请，

sentences.en: because his life is not going to be any less hectic
sentences.zh: 因为两个月后的生活，

sentences.en: two months from now.
sentences.zh: 并不会比现在轻松多少。

sentences.en: Preserving bandwidth takes conscious effort.
sentences.zh: 保护心智带宽需要有意识的努力。

sentences.en: Most of us, Eldar included,
sentences.zh: 我们大多数人，包括埃尔达在内，

sentences.en: are going to violate the Eldar rule.
sentences.zh: 都会违反埃尔达规则。

sentences.en: We'll say yes to new commitments
sentences.zh: 我们会在没有时间的时候，

sentences.en: when we don't have the time
sentences.zh: 答应新的承诺，

sentences.en: or pull out a credit card when we can't afford it.
sentences.zh: 或者在负担不起的时候刷信用卡。

sentences.en: In those moments, it's important to look up,
sentences.zh: 在那些时刻，重要的是抬起头来，

sentences.en: to notice we are inside a tunnel.
sentences.zh: 意识到我们正身处隧道之中。

sentences.zh: 由塔拉·博伊尔剪辑。

sentences.en: Our unsung hero this week is Sung Kim.
sentences.zh: 本周的幕后英雄是成金（Sung Kim）。

sentences.en: Sung is a senior director with the Local Initiative Support Coalition.
sentences.zh: 成金是地方倡议支持联盟的高级主管。

sentences.en: This is a national group that supports financial opportunity centers
sentences.zh: 这是一个支持全国各地金融机会中心的全国性组织，

sentences.en: around the country, including the one in Detroit,
sentences.zh: 包括底特律的那一家，

sentences.en: that helped Brandi Drew get back on her feet.
sentences.zh: 正是它帮助布兰迪·德鲁重新站稳了脚跟。

sentences.en: Sung got us in touch with Brandi
sentences.zh: 成金帮我们联系上了布兰迪，

sentences.en: after making numerous calls
sentences.zh: 他拨打了无数个电话，

sentences.en: and reaching out to friends, colleagues, and counselors.
sentences.zh: 并联络了朋友、同事和顾问。

sentences.en: Sometimes, the people whose stories need telling
sentences.zh: 有时，那些需要被讲述故事的人，

sentences.en: can be hard to find.
sentences.zh: 很难找到。

sentences.en: Sung helped us to bridge that gap.
sentences.zh: 成金帮我们架起了这座桥梁。
